fragment: Typical weight of a mature male lion is 330–550 lb (about 150–250 kg). #lion #lion-facts
Typical weight of a mature lioness is 264–400 lb, somewhat less than a mature male lion. #lion #lion-facts
Lions can sprint up to about 50 mph (80 km/h) and are ambush predators relying on strength, speed and coordinated tactics. #lion #lion-hunting
Lions are crepuscular: most active at dawn and dusk, and also hunt at night thanks to good low-light eyesight; darkness gives them camouflage and reduces detection by prey. #lion #lion-hunting

Lions are social and live in prides of several adult females, their cubs and one or more dominant males; lionesses do most of the hunting cooperatively, surrounding prey and isolating weaker herd members. #lion #lion-hunting #lion-pride

Hunting in a pride lets lions take down large, dangerous prey such as wildebeest and buffalo that a single lion could not handle; solitary hunting, usually by older males, also occurs. #lion #lion-hunting
Lions are territorial: a pride defends its range against other prides, male lions actively fight off rival males, and lionesses patrol the territory, especially in breeding season. #lion #lion-pride
When a new male takes over a pride he kills the previous male's cubs so the females will mate with him. #lion #lion-pride

On 2023/03/08 the user asked about the paper "MoDL: Model Based Deep Learning Architecture for Inverse Problems" — i.e. they're interested in deep-learning approaches to inverse problems. #modl #inverse-problems #user-interests

MoDL (Model-Based Deep Learning) solves inverse problems by unrolling a physics-based forward model into the network, jointly optimizing network weights and model parameters, using a multi-layer/unrolled architecture, and training end-to-end on measurement data. #modl #inverse-problems

MoDL claims improved reconstruction accuracy and faster convergence vs. Tikhonov regularization and other traditional solvers, plus robustness to model mismatch and generalizability across MRI, CT, X-ray crystallography, and audio source separation. #modl #inverse-problems

MoDL tradeoffs discussed: dependence on an accurate physics-based model (model mismatch hurts accuracy), high training-data requirements (an issue in medical imaging), and costly hyperparameter tuning. #modl

Equations discussed for MoDL context: forward model y = Ax + n; inverse problem x̂ = argmin_x L(x,y,A); MSE loss L = ||y − Ax̂||²₂; Tikhonov-regularized version L = ||y − Ax̂||²₂ + λ||x̂||²₂. #modl #inverse-problems
